pairs.difference: A: the glass is almost all light grey, sitting on a dark blue field with a lighter floor band. The hero is clearly separated by value. B: the sky and railing are close to white, and the binocular head is a middle-dark mass with crisp dark lens rings, much like the bright-sky airplane card. Each card has one field slightly outside the real range (A's vignette, B's mean and gap). Neither shows the lesson tells: no added glow behind the hero, no black mass inside the hero.

A: the witch hat reads as one solid near-black mass with hard edges on a middle-grey ring background. Its only light is the buckle and a thin rim streak. The hero/background gap of -0.38 is darker than any real card, and contrast is above the real range. B: the cap is also dark, but a light-grey halo sits behind it, and the gold band and tassel break the mass into a lighter lower edge.
pairs.fix: Paint the hat in mid-tone purples, not near-black. Give the cone and brim a soft lit side with gradual falloff, and keep the darkest shadow to a thin band under the brim.

pairs.difference: B: a stage built from light and dark. Near-black trusses run down both edges and across the top, white spotlight cones cut through, and the floor has a bright pool. The corners are darker than the centre (vignette -0.10, out of range), and contrast is at the top of the range. A: the seahorse is middle values against a soft two-tone blue background, with gentle local contrast and no deep blacks.
pairs.fix: Replace the dark stage with a simple, evenly lit backdrop of soft middle values. Drop the black trusses and spotlight beams, and light the guitar softly from the front.

pairs.difference: A: the cat is a nearly pure-black silhouette filling the centre of a light grey wall and floor. The hero/background gap of -0.50 and contrast of 0.24 are far beyond any real card. The only lights are the eye whites. B: the fountain is all high values on a light ground, with gentle local contrast.
pairs.fix: Make the cat a soft charcoal-grey with clearly lit fur on the top of the head, back and chest, so it reads as a mid-dark shape rather than a black hole. Keep the deepest dark to the shadow under the body.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin is almost the same middle grey as the grass and hedges, with only a slightly darker right face and a light cross. The card reads as one flat middle tone (contrast 0.096, below the real range). B: the stone table and stools are clear light shapes, set against dark tree shadows and cast shadows on the grass.
pairs.fix: Light the coffin's front face clearly brighter than the grass, put a darker side face and a crisp dark cast shadow behind it, and lighten the sky so the card has distinct light, middle and dark areas.

pairs.difference: B: the brightest values on the card are the lit eyes and mouth, which glow almost white inside a middle-grey pumpkin. Dark wood planks fill the lower half, and the face sits lighter than the background (gap 0.167, out of range). A: the duck is a light mass against alternating light and dark rays, the same treatment as the real lamp-post card.
pairs.fix: Keep the carved face only a little brighter than the orange skin, not glowing white. Lighten the wooden floor to a warm middle tone, and put a soft light sunburst behind the pumpkin.

pairs.difference: B: the purple background is almost one flat middle grey with barely visible rays (contrast 0.078, below range). The candles are near-white sticks, and the gold metal is chrome-like, with tight bright and dark streaks. A: a strong light sunburst behind the lamp, darker corners, and a bright chimney glow. That is heavy, but it is the same ray structure as the real sunburst cards.
pairs.fix: Give the background clear light and dark sunburst rays with a brighter centre behind the candelabra. Tone the candles to warm cream rather than pure white, and shade the brass with broad soft gradients instead of thin chrome streaks.

pairs.difference: B matches the real lighthouse card exactly: the dark red band and lantern deck against a light sky and clouds. A: the house is a middle-grey block whose window panes go to pure white, scattered like spots, with dark roofs and dark tree crowns. The light accents are spread across the hero instead of grouped into one mass.
pairs.fix: Draw the windows as warm middle-light panes, not bright white. Light one side of the house as a single brighter plane and keep the roofs a mid-dark purple, so the house reads as two or three large value shapes.

pairs.difference: A: the headstone is a flat middle-grey slab with blotchy, noisy shading, on a near-white floor and a light wall. The overall key is too high (0.761), the corners are brighter than the centre (vignette -0.033, out of range), and the stone barely separates from the wall. B: the sneakers are dark blue against a light floor, with clear white soles and crisp local contrast.
pairs.fix: Shade the headstone with a clearly lit front face and a darker side and top bevel, using smooth gradients instead of speckle. Darken the wall slightly toward the top corners so the stone stands out by value.

pairs.difference: B: the wavy background collapses to a single middle grey, and the broom handle is the same middle value as that grey. Only the bristle head is lighter, and contrast across the card is very low (0.069). A: the red scarf is a dark mass with a light swirl halo behind it and a light medallion at its centre, a clear figure against the background.
pairs.fix: Make the background waves alternate between clearly light and clearly darker blues. Make the broom handle darker or lighter than the waves along its whole length, with a strong lit edge and a darker shadow side.

pairs.difference: A: the cauldron is a solid black body on a dark purple floor. The overall key is too low (0.536), and the only lights are the bright green brew and a small fire under the pot. This is dark-setting, spot-lit staging. B: the gloves are middle values with soft highlights and a light wooden floor. Its corners are also darker than the centre, but its overall key and contrast stay in range.
pairs.fix: Lighten the floor and wall to soft middle values. Paint the cauldron as dark purple, not black, with a broad lit side, and keep the brew only moderately brighter than the rim.

pairs.difference: B: the crystal ball is filled with busy light-and-mid swirls and sharp white specks. The gold stand has tight chrome-style bright and dark streaks, and a dark wood shelf runs along the bottom. The hero's internal contrast is broken up instead of grouped. A: a very light glass on a dark diamond-pattern wall. The gap is high (0.257), but the glass is one clean light mass.
pairs.fix: Fill the ball with one soft, gently brightening glow and a single large highlight, and drop the busy swirls. Shade the brass base with broad smooth gradients, and lighten the wooden shelf to a warm middle tone.

pattern: Generated cards stage light like a horror scene, while the real cards keep a bright, high, even key with soft roll-off. Four signs give them away. First, the hero becomes a near-black silhouette (cat, witch hat, cauldron) that pushes the hero/background gap past -0.3. Second, inner glows go to bright white inside a dark body (pumpkin face, candles, cauldron brew). Third, dark settings with darker corners appear (stage trusses, dark floors). Fourth, the opposite failure: the hero sits in the same middle grey as a flat background (coffin, broom, headstone), so contrast falls below the real range. Smaller tells are chrome-like streaky shading on metal and bright accents scattered across the hero instead of grouped into one mass.
